title: EOD4ECCCH kicks off at the Moravian Library in Brno
content:
TheeBooks-on-Demand (EOD) network gathered at the Moravian Library in Brno, Czechia, on the 8th–9th October 2026 for the first meeting of EOD4ECCCH, a new project supported through the ECHOES Cascading Grants Programme. The meeting explored how libraries can unlock the potential of digitised collections and connect them with the European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage (ECCCH).

Kick-off meeting participants

The EOD network brings together 35 libraries with millions of digitised pages spanning five centuries and several languages. EOD4ECCCH builds on this shared resource, shifting the focus from digitisation to the discovery, enrichment and reuse of digital texts for research, education and public engagement.

The project builds on two decades of experience in digitisation and optical character recognition (OCR), as well as the results of the Creative Europe-funded EODOPEN project in resolving copyright questions, creating accessible formats and involving communities. Its next step is to help libraries use the tools, knowledge and opportunities for cooperation offered by ECHOES and the Cultural Heritage Cloud.

title: HERITWIN launches Newsletter
content:
HERITWIN, which is running five large-scale pilots in Sweden, Norway, Spain, The UK (Northern Ireland), and Greece has launched their first Newsletter! This will be published every three months and  contains news and insights about the project, its activities and progress.

HERITWIN advances the use of semantic digital twins and eXtended Reality reconstructions  to support conservation, education, public engagement, tourism, and interoperable European data spaces. The five pilots which will test the integration of workflows, reusable frameworks, educational resources and more in the ECCCH are:

The MS Henrik Ibsen on the Telemark Canal

Camino de Santiago

  • Stockholm Exhibition (1930) Reconstruction – reconstructs fragmented multilingual collections held by museums, archives and research centres collaborate using digital twins, AI-driven metadata enrichment, adaptive content and federated workflows.
  • Telemark Canal Preparedness – monitoring and predictive control in a real heritage environment. Digital twins model risks such as humidity spikes, flooding and emergency evacuations, while AI supports hazard mitigation, adaptive regulation and stability control

title: ECHOES features in Europeana Project Month on 17th November
content:
ECHOES will feature in the Europeana Project Month webinar series along with Sister projects INFINITY and ECHOLOT  in “Bridging the data space and the ECCCH” on Tuesday the 17th November. Sister project HERITALISE will also feature in the webinar “3D Digitisation” from 14:00-16:00 on Tuesday 10th November.

The webinar will introduce the project, present the latest progress achieved by ECHOES, and demonstrate how the project is building an open, federated ecosystem that connects institutions, datasets, tools and expertise across Europe. A key focus will be on the relationship between the Cultural Heritage Cloud and the Common European Data Space for Cultural Heritage.

Moderator/Chair: Claudio Prandoni, ARIADNE RI

10:00-10:20 – Introduction: Why a Cultural Heritage Cloud? (Xavier Rodier, CNRS, ECHOES Project Coordinator)

Introduction to the vision behind the Cultural Heritage Cloud and the challenges it seeks to address, setting the scene for the session and for the wider Cloud ecosystem.

10:20-10:40 – Building and engaging the Cultural Heritage Cloud community (Rémi Petitcol, FSP)

title: ECHOES showcases CHPortal at SWOCH 2026
content:
SWODCH 2026 is the sixth edition of the International Workshop on Semantic Web and Ontology Design for Cultural Heritage which took place on the 26th October in Bari, Italy, as part of the 25th International Semantic Web Conference (ISWC 2026).

SWODCH is a series of annual conferences whose purpose is to gather original research on the design of conceptual models, ontologies, and Semantic Web (SW) technologies for Cultural Heritage (CH). The heterogeneous and multi-format data available in these domains call for principled methodologies and technologies to semantically characterise, integrate, and reason over data, as well as to support its retrieval, management, analysis, and visualisation. The workshop also welcomes studies addressing the philosophical and social analysis of CH data and knowledge representation models, as ontologies in this domain need to account for the historical and social dimensions of data. SWODCH aims to bring together stakeholders – scholars from Computer Science and the Humanities and GLAM professionals, representatives from CH institutions, etc. – who are involved in the development and deployment of concrete solutions for Cultural Heritage.

title: MusicSphere releases new video on first Use Case
content:
On 2nd–3rd June 2026, the MusicSphere consortium gathered in Thessaloniki, Greece, for its first Use Case Meeting, hosted by the International Hellenic University (IHU) and LUTHIEROS. The visit brought partners closer to the rich heritage of ancient and modern pipe organs, with visits to the Greek Evangelical Church of Katerini, the Archaeological Museum of Dion, and the SEIKILO Museum of Ancient Music.

At the heart of the visit was the Hydraulis of Dion, an extraordinary ancient Greek water-powered organ and the focus of MusicSphere’s first use case. Partners explored its historical significance and the challenges of reconstructing an instrument that has survived only in fragments. Through 3D reconstruction, digital twins, acoustic modelling, artificial intelligence and immersive technologies, MusicSphere aims to bring this remarkable piece of musical heritage closer to researchers and the public, exploring how it may have looked, functioned and sounded in the ancient world. The second day focused on project progress, technical developments and collaboration, helping lay the foundations for the Hydraulis of Dion Digital Twin.

title: ECCCH-ACCESS Project Kick-off in Ankara
content:
Held in Ankara on the 2nd October 2026, the ECCCH-ACCESS Project Kick-Off introduced the project’s aim to connect cultural heritage institutions in Turkey (Türkiye) with the European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage (ECCCH) ecosystem.

Coordinated by Koç University Suna Kıraç Library and KARMA Lab, in partnership with MÜZEDER, Europa Nostra Türkiye, and Ankara AKS, the event featured presentations introducing the ECHOES consortium and the ECCCH approach, followed by a panel exploring experiences and practices in cultural heritage digitisation in Turkey.

The ECCCH process

ECCCH-ACCESS combines four complementary components:

  • awareness and community expansion through webinars and outreach activities;
  • sector mapping and feedback collection through surveys and moderated discussions;
  • knowledge translation through a dedicated website, multilingual training materials, and
  • AI-assisted dissemination; and participatory engagement through hackathons and co-design sessions.

    • Activities will engage museums, archaeological projects, libraries, researchers, and heritage professionals across Turkey through established institutional and professional networks.

title: ECHOES at the NEMO European Museum Conference
content:
Last week, ECHOES partners attended the NEMO European Museum Conference entitled Human after all – Museums in the wake of AI in Vilnius (11th-13th October), Lithuania, and organised a workshop dedicated to Nordic and Baltic cultural heritage professionals on the 14th October. This session invited museum professionals, researchers and policy makers to present their national and regional landscapes, and explore new opportunities for knowledge exchange and collaboration in a complex political and technological context.

During the first half of the workshop, the audience was introduced to the ECHOES project and the Cloud, including detailed presentations of the community engagement activities by FSP and a demonstration of the Cloud’s features and infrastructure design by PCSS. The second half of the session was dedicated to a round table gathering museum professionals from Northen Europe. They were invited to present their national cultural and policy landscape and discuss how the Cloud could support better collaboration beyond national and regional frameworks.

An important output from the NEMO Conference was their statement on AI and Museums, download the PDF here.

title: COLOURS, UNICHE, PlaceMUS XR and StratiGraph at BMTA Paestum
content:
COLOURS and fellow Sister projects UNICHE, PlaceMUS XR and StratiGraph will present their digital tools for coloured heritage at a joint workshop organised at the XXVIII Borsa Mediterranea del Turismo Archeologico (BMTA) in Paestum, Italy from 13:00-15:00 on the 29th October.

The aim of the New digital tools and EU funding for museums and heritage workshop which is designed for museums, heritage institutions, conservators-restorers, heritage scientists and other professionals, is to show what these tools can do in practice. Participants can see concrete examples, learn about the projects’ open calls and test the tools directly with the people who develop them.

It is also a good opportunity for organisations interested in applying to the COLOURS and UNICHE open calls. The session is free but registration is appreciated for planning purposes.

Please see the COLOURS website for the programme and further details about the workshop.
